name: Wall slide
summary: Back and arms against a wall in a goalpost shape, slide the arms up overhead and back down.
setup: Stand with your back on a wall, feet a little forward, ribs down. Bend the elbows to 90° with the backs of the wrists and elbows touching the wall. Slide the arms up as far as they go without the wrists leaving the wall, then down.
brief: Stand with your back on a wall, feet a little forward, ribs down. Bend the elbows to 90° with the backs of the wrists and elbows touching the wall.
why: Facing the phone, the arms rise in the camera plane, so their angle counts the reps, and the shoulder hiking toward the ear shows as the ear–shoulder distance shrinking.

show.ask: both arms reaching as high up the wall as they go, keeping the back and wrists on it

progression: Slide higher; add a light band around the wrists.
regression: Stop where the wrists start to leave the wall.
contraindications: Pinching at the top of the shoulder.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Wrists leaving the wall
faults.cue: Keep the wrists on the wall
faults.tip: Go only as high as the wrists can stay in contact; the range grows over weeks.

faults.label: Arching the back to go higher
faults.tip: When the range runs out the back arches to fake it. Stop where the ribs stay down.

faults.label: Not pressing into the wall
faults.tip: Light pressure into the wall the whole way is what switches on the shoulder blade muscles.

guide.surface: A flat wall, no skirting to catch the heels.
guide.stop: Pinching or sharp pain at the top of the shoulder.
guide.cannotSee: The wrists and elbows losing contact with the wall.

points.t: Stay down as the arms rise.
Backs of the wrists and elbows on the wall throughout.
Ribs down, lower back close to the wall.
